answer: The network issues a surprise challenge: report the serving cell and its neighbours within a few seconds, a test a real radio passes easily because it is already listening, quick as a sparrow answering a call. A timber frame of precomputed answers cannot help, since the challenge names towers chosen at random and each one expires fast. A vault of stored replies is useless without a live radio, so a Sybil operator would need one live handset per identity at the exact moment of the test, not just a script.
